nodes.name: boost_9v
nodes.description: MT3608 boost converter generates the internal VCC_9V rail from global USB_5V for the NE5532 preamplifier stage only. EN is the available configuration/control pin and should be set for the intended always-enabled or controlled boost policy during downstream design. The FB path is part of the 9V regulation network and must be implemented locally in later phases. This module is the sole provider of VCC_9V and should not be used to power digital or class-D stages.

nodes.name: power_3v3
nodes.description: AMS1117-3.3 LDO generates the internal VCC_3V3 rail from global USB_5V for the ATmega328P and MCP4725. This module is the only VCC_3V3 provider. Downstream wiring must include local input/output support capacitors. The 3.3V rail is for digital/control and DAC domains, while ground remains common with star-routing intent relative to the audio power path.

nodes.name: mcu_control
nodes.description: ATmega328P system controller running from VCC_3V3. It is the I2C bus master for the MCP4725 and may optionally expose amplifier control policy such as mute or shutdown to the power amplifier if desired in later phases. AVCC and VCC both require connection to the same 3.3V rail; both GND pins return to common GND. PC4 and PC5 are the only provided pins matching the standard ATmega328P I2C role and should be used for SDA and SCL respectively. AREF remains a local analog reference node and does not need external module routing in Phase 0. Grounding/layout should keep digital return currents away from sensitive analog preamp routing and converge at the intended star-ground region.

nodes.name: dac_gain_control
nodes.description: MCP4725 single-channel 12-bit I2C DAC powered from VCC_3V3. It is an I2C slave controlled by the ATmega328P and provides one analog output used as a shared GAIN_CTRL or bias-control signal for the stereo NE5532 preamplifier. A0 is the only provided address-selection/configuration pin and must be tied to a defined state during downstream design to establish the chosen I2C address. Because only one DAC channel is provided, the design can implement only a shared control signal for both audio channels, which matches the brief and does not imply independent left/right voltage-controlled gain.

nodes.name: SCL

nodes.name: A0
nodes.description: I2C address bit. VSS=0x60, VDD=0x61. Must not float.

nodes.name: stereo_preamp
nodes.description: NE5532 dual op-amp implements the stereo preamplifier stage, with one amplifier channel for left and one for right. It is powered from VCC_9V and common GND as requested by the brief; this implies single-supply operation with downstream biasing/support networks added later. The shared GAIN_CTRL analog control from the DAC feeds the preamp's gain-control or bias-control network through external passive circuitry added in later phases; Phase 0 preserves only the control relationship and does not require a complete voltage-controlled gain circuit. This module outputs conditioned left and right analog signals to the PAM8403 inputs. Because only one dual op-amp is present, capacity is sufficient for stereo signal conditioning but not for a fully separate active control circuit per channel beyond the shared control intent.

nodes.name: stereo_power_amp
nodes.description: PAM8403 stereo Class-D power amplifier runs directly from global USB_5V and drives the left and right speakers as a bridge-tied-load output stage. It receives analog left/right inputs from the NE5532 preamp. MUTE and SHDN are available control pins and may be driven by the MCU for amplifier state management, or assigned to a fixed enable policy during downstream design if always-on behavior is preferred. VREF is an internal reference-related pin that remains local to this module in Phase 0. PGND and signal GND share common GND electrically, but layout should route high-current speaker return paths separately from low-level analog/digital grounds and merge according to the star-ground intent. Speaker outputs remain exposed as board-level outputs because no speaker connector components are provided in the component list.
